Corporate.tagline: Multi-specialty primary care and ambulatory services.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Coombe is a surname pulled from older medical practice naming — quiet, slightly Anglo-Irish, professional. Medical Partners signals the partner-led organizational structure. The pair reads as a long-standing physician group, not a venture-funded clinic chain.
Corporate.manifesto: Coombe Medical Partners is a physician-owned multi-specialty group serving primary care, internal medicine, and ambulatory services across multiple sites. The buyer is a health system, an employer benefits team, or a regional payer. The relationship is the multi-year contract. The metric is patient outcomes and operational reliability.
Corporate.industrySummary: Multi-specialty physician groups face consolidation pressure from health systems and private equity. The opening is for a physician-owned group with operational depth, integrated billing, and quality metrics that hold up to payer scrutiny.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Privia Health (priviahealth.com) is the platform reference. Iora Health (iorahealth.com) holds the value-based peer slot. ChenMed (chenmed.com) plays in the senior-care middle. We sit in the regional physician-owned multi-specialty category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Coombe Medical Partners is a physician-owned multi-specialty group operating primary care and ambulatory services across a regional footprint.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on quality metrics, payer contract performance, and physician retention. The group is owned by the physicians, not by a platform.

Want a partner whose physicians stay long-term.

Publish a quarterly group performance review.
Refer to the physicians by name in correspondence.

Corporate.brandDescription: Aldgate Health Holdings operates a portfolio of healthcare brands across primary care, specialty practice, urgent care, and digital health categories.
Corporate.scope:
Aldgate Health Holdings works across:
• Multi-brand healthcare clinic operations
• Shared clinical staff credentialing across jurisdictions
• Payer contracting and billing infrastructure
• Real-estate portfolio for clinic locations
• Annual investor and operator reporting
Corporate.mission: To provide a serious operating platform for mid-tier healthcare brands that want to keep their identity and outsource the operations.
Corporate.vision: A healthcare operator whose portfolio brands grow under their own names because the credentialing and contracting are shared.
coreValues: Senior — partners deal with partners.
Operational — credentialing and contracting run on schedule.
Reliable — clinicians stay because operations are stable.
Discreet — clinic and payer relationships stay private.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Aldgate is a real London place-name with a heritage trade register. Health Holdings follows the multi-brand operator naming convention used in healthcare (HCA Healthcare, Ascension, Optum Health structure). The pair reads as an institutional operator with multi-brand portfolio scale.
Corporate.manifesto: Aldgate Health Holdings owns and operates a portfolio of healthcare clinic brands. Each clinic retains its clinical leadership, patient base, and brand identity; we operate the shared credentialing, billing, and back office. The buyer is a clinic founder considering sale, a payer seeking single-vendor contracting, or an institutional investor holding healthcare assets.
Corporate.industrySummary: Healthcare clinic operations have consolidated under a small number of multi-brand operators (HCA, Ascension, CVS Health). The opening is for a regional mid-tier multi-brand operator with deep credentialing operations.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Optum Health (optum.com) is the multi-brand healthcare reference. Privia Health (priviahealth.com) holds the multi-brand peer slot. Aledade (aledade.com) sits in the multi-practice peer position. Oak Street Health (oakstreethealth.com) plays the modern multi-clinic peer reference. We belong in the regional mid-tier multi-brand healthcare operator category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Aldgate Health Holdings is a regional multi-brand healthcare operator running clinic operations, credentialing, payer contracting, and shared compliance across a portfolio of healthcare brands.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on shared credentialing depth, payer contracting reach, and the procurement-grade reliability healthcare brand founders and payers require.

targetAudience.primary: Healthcare clinic founders considering sale, payer contracting leads, and institutional investors holding healthcare assets.

Negotiate multi-payer contracts.
Care about MLR, payer mix, and clinician retention.
Renew on multi-year operating terms.
motivations: Need an operator with shared credentialing.
Need to keep clinic identity post-acquisition.
Need shared payer contracting.

dos: Lead with clinic portfolio, payer footprint, and clinician retention.
Speak the language of clinic founders, payers, and compliance officers.
Publish quarterly operator letters.
Refer to clinics by name, not by Aldgate tagging.
donts: No consumer-facing marketing in the holding voice.
No social-media presence at the parent level.
No clinic consolidation announcements without partner alignment.

Creative.tagline: A clinic for the people who travel to patients.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Bedside is the trade term for caring presence with a patient. Care is the plain category word; Co the small-firm suffix. Stands in the lineage of considered-creative healthcare brands.
Creative.manifesto: Most healthcare brands sound like an insurance company trying to be your friend. They overpromise, underexplain, and outsource the warmth. House Call is the brand for the doctor who knows your name, has been to your kitchen, and won't pretend the system is fine. Warm, sharp, honest about what's broken.
Creative.industrySummary: Healthcare branding has been polished, professional, and a little cold. There's room for one that's warm, personable, sticker-friendly, and still serious about the work.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Parsley Health (parsleyhealth.com) does warm-modern. Tia (asktia.com) holds the design-forward women's health position. Galileo (galileo.io) sits in the digital-first peer group. We sit warmer than all of them, with a clearer point of view.
Creative.positioningStatement: A primary care brand that treats the patient like a person, not a chart.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Has insurance, doesn't trust it. Already pays out of pocket for at least one health service. Wants the doctor to actually know them. Will pay for the relationship.

dos: Talk like the family doctor who would call you back
Be honest about what's broken in the system
Make jokes about the bureaucracy

Creative.tagline: A clinic that runs to time.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Treatment Room is the trade name for the working consultation space. The definite article gives the brand the register of a named small clinic.
Creative.manifesto: We made The Treatment Room because waiting rooms are the lie at the heart of healthcare. You arrive at the appointment time. You wait forty minutes. The visit lasts twelve minutes. We started a clinic that flips the math. The waiting room has six chairs and is mostly empty. If we are running late, we say so before you arrive and we credit the visit fee.
Creative.industrySummary: Patient satisfaction surveys consistently identify wait time as the largest source of clinic frustration. No clinic brand has chosen wait time as its primary positioning. There is a real opening for a brand that competes on the waiting-room metric.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Forward (goforward.com) touches operational efficiency. One Medical (onemedical.com) holds the modern-experience slot. Crossover Health (crossoverhealth.com) is the employer-onsite peer. We sit further out — the brand is the clock.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Treatment Room is a clinic that runs to time and credits the visit fee when it does not.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand makes a public promise about wait time and stakes the visit fee on it. The clinic is operationally built around the promise.

targetAudience.primary: Working adults who have stopped going to the doctor because of how long it takes.
behaviors: Schedule visits around their work calendar.
Resent waiting rooms.
Avoid annual physicals.

motivations: Want a clinic that respects their calendar.
Want a visit that starts on time.
Want a clinic willing to bet on its own promise.

dos: State the promise plainly.
Publish wait-time data weekly.
Notify patients in advance if running late.
Use the brand line — 'no waiting' — on every door.
donts: No magazines in the waiting room — there is no waiting room to fill.

Creative.tagline: A clinic where the waiting room is the work.
Creative.brandDescription: The Waiting Room Co is a creative-led primary-care clinic that treats the waiting room — the space between booking and visit — as a primary design and operational object, with intentional waiting-room programming.
Creative.scope:
The Waiting Room Co works across:
• Primary-care clinics with intentional waiting-room programming
• Reading materials curated by a programming editor
• No screens, no piped music, no clinical-poster sprawl
• Quarterly published essays on the waiting-room tradition
• Annual clinic update for patients
Creative.mission: To restore the waiting room as a considered space rather than an afterthought.
Creative.vision: A clinic whose waiting rooms become a small cultural reference for how clinical spaces can be made.
coreValues: Warm — the waiting room is part of the visit.
Specific — every chair, every magazine, every detail is chosen.
Considered — the design is intentional.
Literary — the writing about clinical space is part of the brand.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Waiting Room is the universal clinical-space phrase for the room between booking and visit — typically treated as utilitarian. Naming the clinic after the waiting room stakes a clear creative position around that space as the central designed object. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school.
Creative.manifesto: Most clinical waiting rooms are designed by accident — TVs, piped music, expired magazines, fluorescent light. We started The Waiting Room Co because the waiting room is part of the care. We design it intentionally — natural light, curated reading, quiet, real seating — and treat the time before the visit as part of the visit.
Creative.industrySummary: Clinical waiting rooms have been treated as utility space. There is real space for a creative-led clinic that positions explicitly on the waiting room as a designed object.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Forward (goforward.com) plays the modern-clinical design peer. Parsley Health (parsleyhealth.com) holds the considered-clinical peer slot. One Medical (onemedical.com) sits in the modern peer position. The CityMD chain plays the urgent-clinical peer reference. We sit alongside Parsley with a sharper waiting-room creative position.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Waiting Room Co is a primary-care clinic chain that treats the waiting room as the primary designed object of the clinical experience.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the waiting-room premise. Every aspect of the clinic is built around the time before the visit.

targetAudience.primary: Patients 28-55 who notice the design of clinical spaces and prefer considered environments for medical visits.
behaviors: Care about the quality of clinical waiting environments.
Read books and articles while waiting.
Skip clinics with poor waiting environments.
Pay full per-visit pricing or membership fees.
motivations: Want a clinic with a considered waiting room.
Want reading material curated thoughtfully.
Want a clinical space that respects their time before the visit.

dos: Publish the quarterly essay on the waiting-room tradition.
Photograph the waiting rooms.
Reference the programming editor and reading-list curator by name.
Sign post-visit notes by the clinician.
donts: No screens or piped music in waiting rooms.
